note: Synthetic Point32Health proof-of-concept data for Predictive Incident Intelligence. Monitoring metrics, the employee directory mapping and the Controlled Demo Mode incident history are simulated. In Live Agent Mode the incident history comes from the POC ServiceNow instance.

deviation.label: Current metric deviation
deviation.how: How far the current readings are from their normal baseline, measured against the critical threshold (worst metric 70%, average of all metrics 30%).

history.label: Historical incident frequency
history.how: Incidents on this service family in the last 90 days (10 or more scores 100).

similar.label: Similar previous incidents
similar.how: Share of similar past incidents that caused a service disruption (priority 1 or 2), scaled down when there are fewer than 5 similar incidents.

criticality.label: Service criticality
criticality.how: Business criticality of the service, 1 to 5.

recurrence.label: Incident recurrence
recurrence.how: Size of the largest cluster of the same problem on the same component (6 or more repeats scores 100).

duration.label: Duration of abnormal behaviour
duration.how: How long the metrics have been abnormal (60 minutes or more scores 100).

rate.label: Rate of change
rate.how: How fast the most deviated signal moved over the last readings, measured against the gap between its baseline and critical threshold.

correlated.label: Correlated signals
correlated.how: How many signal categories (infrastructure, application, database, network, business, user experience, capacity) are abnormal at the same time (5 or more scores 100).

business.label: Business impact
business.how: The service's business impact level (1-5), raised when its business-transaction signals are also abnormal.

changes.label: Recent changes
changes.how: A change, deployment or configuration event in the last 48 hours that touches the abnormal signals (suspected contributor, never a confirmed cause). More recent scores higher.

capacity.label: Capacity forecast
capacity.how: How soon the forecast says the service reaches its capacity limit (now scores 100; a week or more away scores 0).

reliability.label: Data reliability
reliability.how: Quality rating of the data sources behind the abnormal signals, scaled by how many independent categories agree. Unreliable or single-source evidence adds little.

directory.note: Synthetic employee directory mapping for the POC: department head counts, remote share and the applications each department depends on. No individual employee records.

rca.title: Predicted SSO sign-in disruption: login failures rising on the identity provider
rca.description: Raised proactively by AURA Predictive Intelligence before any employee report. Login failures rose from about 10 to 45 per hour and authentication response time from 350 ms to 1.9 s over the last 35 minutes. Similar past incidents on sso-lb-04 led to sign-in outages.
rca.business_impact: All employees could be unable to sign in to Microsoft 365, the Employee Center and business applications.
rca.complexity: Multi-agent: needs a second evidence round

logs.text: Login failures climbed from 10/hour to 45/hour; failures cite 'token signature validation failed'.
Health checks pass on all four identity provider nodes behind sso-lb-04.

changes.title: Identity provider token-signing certificate rotation
changes.detail: New signing certificate published; nodes updated by rolling restart.

history.title: Expired TLS certificate on sso-lb-04
history.resolution: Certificate renewed on the load-balanced node.

kb.title: Token-signing certificate rotation
kb.summary: Every IdP node must load the new signing key; a node that misses the restart keeps signing with the old key.

deep.text: 97% of failed sign-ins were served by idp-node-3; the other three nodes are clean.
idp-node-3 is still signing tokens with the previous certificate thumbprint; its restart in CHG-DEMO-7101 was skipped.

hypotheses.title: One identity provider node is signing tokens with the old certificate after the rotation
hypotheses.why: Failures cite signature validation and started after the rotation change.

hypotheses.title: Load balancer sso-lb-04 sending traffic to an unhealthy node
DNS resolution failure for the SSO endpoint

critic: Fits the timing, but which node? Need per-node failure split and certificate inventory.
Health checks pass on all nodes (L2), so the load balancer is routing correctly.
DNS failures would stop all sign-ins, not a fraction with signature errors.
script.root_cause: The token-signing certificate rotation (CHG-DEMO-7101) skipped the restart of idp-node-3, which keeps signing tokens with the retired certificate, so about a quarter of sign-ins routed to it fail signature validation.
contributing: Rolling restart had no post-check that every node serves the new thumbprint.
Load balancer health checks don't test token signing.

remediation.expected: No new sign-ins reach the stale node.

remediation.step: Restart idp-node-3 so it loads the new signing certificate.
Return idp-node-3 to the pool and watch sign-in failures for 15 minutes.
remediation.expected: Login failures back under 20 per hour.

script.rollback: Keep idp-node-3 drained; three nodes carry normal load.
prevention: Add a certificate thumbprint check to the rotation runbook.
Extend health checks to validate a signed test token.

live_signal.label: ServiceNow sign-in events (live)

actions: Check where the failed sign-ins come from and whether they target real accounts.

rca.description: Raised proactively by AURA Predictive Intelligence before any employee report. Payment API response time rose from 200 ms to about 2 s and HTTP 504 errors to 38 per hour over the last 90 minutes. The same pattern preceded several past Payment API outages.

changes.detail: Idle TCP session timeout lowered from 60 to 30 minutes.

history.title: Payment API returning HTTP 504 after idle period

kb.title: Gateway connection pooling
kb.summary: Pool idle eviction must be shorter than any firewall idle timeout on the path.

hypotheses.title: Firewall drops idle pooled connections that the gateway still reuses
hypotheses.why: 504s only after idle periods; the firewall idle timeout was just lowered below the pool eviction time.

hypotheses.title: Payments database connection pool exhausted
hypotheses.why: A past incident had this cause.

hypotheses.title: Network latency on the gateway path

critic: Evidence directly shows stale pooled connections failing after the firewall change.
New connections succeed, so the pool isn't exhausted.
Latency is only high on the first request after idle.
script.root_cause: The firewall change CHG-DEMO-7204 cut the idle TCP timeout to 30 minutes while pay-gw-04 keeps pooled upstream connections for 60 minutes, so reused stale connections hang until the 45-second timeout and return HTTP 504.
contributing: Pool eviction time not reviewed when the firewall policy changed.
No keep-alive on gateway upstream connections.

remediation.step: Set the gateway pool idle eviction to 20 minutes on pay-gw-04.
remediation.expected: No pooled connection outlives the firewall timeout.

remediation.step: Enable TCP keep-alive on upstream connections.
remediation.expected: Idle connections stay open through the firewall.
Stale connections cleared; response time under 600 ms.

script.rollback: Restore the previous gateway pool settings.
prevention: Add pool and keep-alive settings to the firewall change checklist.
Alert on first-request latency after idle.

kb.title: VPN client profiles
kb.summary: The re-authentication interval is set in the client profile; the default in 7.4.x is 10 minutes.

hypotheses.title: VPN client 7.4.2 re-authenticates every 10 minutes and floods the gateway and RADIUS
hypotheses.why: Re-auth storm from 7.4.2 clients matches the rise in sessions and RADIUS timeouts.

critic: Logs tie the load to the 7.4.2 re-auth behaviour.
CPU follows session count; no hardware errors.
script.root_cause: The VPN client 7.4.2 rollout (CHG-DEMO-7420) ships a 10-minute re-authentication default, so 1,100 laptops re-authenticate constantly, filling the vpn-gw-01 session table and overloading RADIUS.
contributing: Client profile not overridden in the rollout package.
No capacity test for the new client.

remediation.step: Push the client profile with an 8-hour re-authentication interval.
remediation.expected: Re-auth rate drops within one cycle.
Session table below 60% and CPU below 60%.

script.rollback: Pause the 7.4.2 rollout and redeploy 7.3.9 to affected laptops.
prevention: Pilot client updates with 50 users first.
Pin client profile settings in the package.

history.title: Workday worker sync failed: integration credential expired

kb.title: Managed integration secrets
kb.summary: Integration credentials should be stored in the vault with automatic rotation.

hypotheses.title: Manually rotated 30-day integration credential will expire again in 4 days
hypotheses.why: Six failures at 30-day intervals; current credential is 26 days old.

critic: Pattern and credential age match exactly.
Every past failure was fixed by a credential rotation, not an API change.
No network errors in past incidents.
script.root_cause: The svc-workday-sync integration uses a manually rotated credential with a 30-day lifetime and no automatic rotation, so the sync fails each time it expires; the current credential expires in about 4 days.
contributing: Previous incidents fixed the symptom (rotation) but no problem record was opened.
No expiry alerting on integration credentials.

remediation.step: Move the credential to the vault with automatic rotation.
Add an expiry alert 7 days before any integration credential expires.

script.rollback: Keep the manual credential in place until vault rotation is proven.
prevention: Open a problem record for repeat incidents.
Inventory all integration credentials for expiry.
